TrixiHyQMOM

A discontinuous Galerkin implementation of the extended Gramian closure for moment equations

Physical Background

  • To-Do

Main Features

  • Solving the 1D(space) - 1D(velocity) moment equations on a Riemann problem
  • Numerical grid convergence
  • Solving the 1D(space) - 1D(velocity) moment equations for the Vlasov-Poisson system with initial conditions:
    • Landau Damping
    • Two-stream instability
  • Extending the equations to 1D(space) - 3D(velocity) for M=4

Installation

First, clone the git repository

git clone git@git.rwth-aachen.de:JanHab/trixihyqmom.git
cd trixihyqmom

We need the Revise julia package to execute most of the scripts. In principle, this is not necessary for the numerical backend, but was used to accelerate implementations.

using Pkg;
Pkg.add(Revise);
Pkg.instantiate()

Now we can install the HyQMOM package locally with:


julia --project
using Pkg;
Pkg.instantiate()
  • ToDo: Test this out!

Testing

Clone the repository and execute the testing pipeline with:

julia test/tests.jl

Usage

Find the package source code in src, which implements the momentum closure and the system of PDEs. The subfolder src/TrixiTree2Triangulation is a subpackage developed by Matthias Geratz for storing the solution in a *.tsv file.

The folder examples contains some main files for physical relevant benchmark problems slurm gives shell scripts for executing the benchmark problems either on your local laptop or on a HPC server with a slurm script. You need to either comment the os.system(command) or createsbatch file, depending on your system.

miscellaneous contains miscellaneous files used for implementation and checking.

notebooks has all the visualizations.

Finally, test has the testing pipeline.
